action: Frank does not make a third phone call to the adult ed coordinator. He goes in person. He drives to the district office during morning business hours, asks for the coordinator by name, and explains briefly that he has called twice and wants five minutes if she has them. If she is available, he hands her the four-module curriculum document and makes one ask: a fifteen-minute meeting within the next two weeks to discuss whether there is a fit between what he has built and what the district's adult ed catalog needs. If she is not available, he leaves the curriculum document with the front desk in a labeled envelope with a handwritten note — his name, Mark Thompson's name as the referral, his phone number, and one line: 'I would like five minutes at your convenience. I have already developed the curriculum.' He does not apologize for showing up. He is a professional with a real product and a real referral. Showing up in person after two unreturned calls is not desperate — it is what people who are serious about their work do.
